correctness.rationale: Every stationary marginal is invariant for the two contracting branches. For finite bias both symbols have uniformly positive probability, giving nonatomicity and full support. Their inverse is the doubling map, whose only absolutely continuous invariant probability is uniform; uniform fails stationarity under logistic bias, so singularity follows from preserved Lebesgue decomposition. Uniformly summable log-probability deviations along all-positive/all-negative histories give exact two-sided cylinder asymptotics and endpoint limits. The no-bias law follows from fair binary digits. Finite checker confirms branch geometry and finite product bounds; no finite experiment is used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: Near-extreme media-opinion tail scaling directly measures how alignment bias concentrates stationary opinions. The exact nonlinear exponent supplies a sharp observable distinction between arbitrarily weak homophily and the unbiased media-only regime, beyond the original deterministic drift threshold and beyond qualitative statements about singular stationary laws. This is a natural boundary observable of the paper's actual logistic choice mechanism, not an arbitrary parameter slice.
